title: Rapid coordination of effective learning by the human hippocampus: intracranial EEG during scene recognition with eye tracking
description: Stereo-EEG recordings from six patients with medically refractory epilepsy performing a scene recognition memory task with concurrent EyeLink eye tracking. The data accompany a study of how the human hippocampus rapidly coordinates effective learning. They were re-packaged losslessly into iEEG-BIDS from the authors' public Zenodo release and include electrode MNI coordinates, behavioral arrays, eye-tracking files and analysis code in sourcedata.
methods_description: Nihon Kohden amplifier recordings at 1 or 2 kHz with AD-TECH depth electrodes, while participants studied and then recognized natural scenes (8 blocks of 24 images). Gaze-contingent viewing at test was recorded with an EyeLink 1000 at 500 Hz. Nihon Kohden ASCII exports were converted losslessly to BrainVision INT_32 format with no filtering, resampling or re-referencing.
